title: Three Nights and One Short Score
subtitle: 音乐之声 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 音乐之声（文学艺术与体育·音乐与表演）
meta: 主题语境：音乐之声（文学艺术与体育·音乐与表演）　|　核心词汇：song　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 song 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1953 the musician ① sang the song that no listener in the hall would have noted, and he said the singing was the whole of the night. The ② song, meaning the tune itself and not the score, ran three nights and stayed unnoted in the book; a song, he said, is the only thing in a hall that is judged by how long it is left unnoted.

Every ③ song in that hall had the same short score beside it, and the ④ song at the far piano, meaning the note they kept for the children to play and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A song, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to note; the musician said the noting is the part that fills three nights.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the song was the whole of the matter, meaning the feeling and not the tune. The ⑥ song, meaning the feeling and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody notes; song, he said, is either something you sing or the only word that means both a tune and a feeling. He said the feeling is the part they remember.

By 1958 the ⑦ song had become a line in a programme, and the programme had become an argument about the short score. The ⑧ song of the whole thing, the musician wrote in December, was one hall and three nights of noting; song, he said, is either the note at the far piano or the reason you learned to note. He said the noting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ song I remember is the tune noted in the programme, which closed in 1960 and is still noted as the quietest in the hall. A ⑩ song, my mother said in 1962, is the only tune that improves by being noted; every song, she said, is a feeling that has agreed to look like a tune. She said the feeling was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 歌；歌曲（指音乐厅里每一首旁边的那一首）
B. n. 歌；歌曲（指那首歌本身，与薄薄的乐谱相对）
C. 固定搭配：sing the song 唱这一首歌
D. n. 歌；歌曲（指留给孩子们弹的那一个）
E. n. 歌之事（抽象总称，指一处音乐厅的歌之事）
F. n. 歌；歌曲（指节目单里写到、被记下的那一首）
G. n. 歌、情思（指一件事里人人都听却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 情思（抽象总称，指人人都听却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: sang the song that no listener in the hall would have noted
The song, meaning the tune itself and not the score
the song at the far piano
the song was the whole of the matter
the song had become a line in a programme
The song of the whole thing
A song, my mother said in 1962

answers.why: sing the song 意为“唱这一首歌”，1953 年那位乐师把音乐厅里没有一位听客肯记下的一首歌做了一遍。
song 意为“歌；歌曲”，指那首歌本身而不是薄薄的乐谱，它经过了三个夜晚而在簿子上没有被记下。
song 意为“歌；歌曲”，指音乐厅里每一首旁边的那一首，每一首旁边都有同一份薄薄的乐谱。
song 意为“歌；歌曲”，指最远那张琴凳的留给孩子们弹的那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
song 意为“歌、情思”，指一件事里人人都听却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这首情思就是那件事的全部。
song 意为“情思”，指人人都听却无人提起的那样东西而不是那首歌，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
song 意为“歌；歌曲”，指节目单里写到、被记下的那一首，到 1958 年这一首成了节目单里的一行。
song 意为“歌之事”，乐师十二月写道，整件事的歌之事是一处音乐厅和三个夜晚的记下。
song 意为“歌；歌曲”，我记得的是节目单里记下过的那一首，1960 年奏完了，至今仍被说成音乐厅里最安静的一首。
song 为抽象总称，母亲 1962 年说，歌是唯一会因为被好好记下而变得更好的歌。
